reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Rebuilt the route from the current catalogue groups and exact code, credit and offering entries. Rechecked both semester choice rules and ruled out Linear Models without prior statistics, then reconsidered the regulations and exact graduation entries before checking the current UCR workbook, each plan and the finished display.
findings: The current BA-URB catalogue and September 2026 OER support an English-taught 180 EC programme. Year one has ten required components. Year two has 30 EC fixed, one 10 EC thematic elective and one 5 EC methods elective per semester. The official public ordering supports Safe City and Sustainable City in their respective terms. Humanities and Urbanism is first-listed for semester one and advised for the neutral Urban Arts, Culture and Society thesis track. Inferential Statistics runs in that same term, and is prerequisite to Linear Models. The first eligible second-semester methodology option after Humanities and Urbanism is therefore Spatial Analysis and Modelling. Year three has a 5 EC literature seminar, a 25 EC graduation track and a 30 EC open block. The chosen track has a 5 EC thesis seminar, 10 EC research lab and 10 EC independent thesis. The environmental graduation project is an alternative to the entire 25 EC thesis track. Optional workplace preparation adds no compulsory credits.

Article 4.2 and the exact lab and seminar pages require 100 EC including two thematic and two methods electives, and Reading the City, for the selected graduation track. Humanities and Urbanism is advised. The exact thesis entry requires the seminar to be completed before thesis work and its approved proposal forms the basis of the independent research. The first semester of year three is the approved elective block; the selected components are in semester two, with the research lab in block three and thesis in block four. The 2026 regulations retain open-choice approval and track-specific entry; no second thesis is counted.

Four invalid UCR placements were resolved with three term swaps. Spatial Planning replaces Soils & Aquifers to give the climate plan more direct GIS and spatial intervention work, without claiming Leiden’s historical planning sequence. The safe and healthy option remains four courses distinct from the governance option, with a substantive health psychology and empirical focus. The 10 EC independent thesis remains separate from UCR’s optional research.
